Title: DAP leader slams opposition boycott of Tabung Haji RCI debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DAP central executive committee member Senator Sheikh Umar Bagharib Ali has criticised opposition members of parliament, who walked out of the Dewan Rakyat, today.
The
walkout came during the debate
on the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji.
The Johor DAP deputy chairman said the move was regrettable as the debate provided MPs an opportunity to scrutinise the
RCI findings
and raise issues concerning Tabung Haji depositors.
"Leaving the Dewan Rakyat while this issue is being debated is not in keeping with the spirit of His Majesty, the King of Malaysia.
"If they genuinely want to seek the truth, the place to do so is at the debate, not by walking out," he said in a statement today.
Sheikh Umar said the RCI report should not be treated as the property of any political party as it concerned an institution entrusted with the savings and interests of millions of Muslims.
He said all MPs, from both sides of the political divide, had a responsibility to scrutinise the findings seriously and ensure weaknesses in governance were not repeated.
"This is not about which side wins or loses politically. This is about trust, governance, the people's money and Tabung Haji depositors.
"And this is about upholding the decree of the His Majesty," he said.

Title: Millions of burnt books show how 'war of endurance' is hurting Ukraine
Article:
VIKTOR Kruhlov, director of Ranok, one of Ukraine's largest children's publishers, struggled to hold back tears as he watched pile after pile of his books turn to ash.
"It's a terrible sight to see books burning," he said.
A Russian drone strike on Ranok's warehouse in the northeastern city of Kharkiv on Aug 1 destroyed about eight million books, the biggest blow yet to Ukraine's publishing industry during the four-year-old war.
Publishers say more than 10 million books have been destroyed in attacks on warehouses in recent months, threatening an industry that initially benefited from rising demand for Ukrainian-language literature at the start of the conflict.
As firefighters battled the blaze, Kruhlov said the first explosion at the warehouse was followed moments later by a second at the same spot.
"This was a deliberately planned attack against the book warehouse," said Kruhlov, whose company prints around one-third of the textbooks used in Ukrainian schools.
Russia's defence ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
The attacks on book warehouses and printing houses have resonated deeply in a country where many see the war as a fight for national survival and identity.
Education Minister Andrii Butenko described them as an attempt to destroy the Ukrainian language, history and memory, "everything from which the identity of our children grows."
Russian President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly questioned Ukraine's separate statehood and argued that Russians and Ukrainians are one people.
Beyond their symbolic impact, the strikes on the publishing industry illustrate the mounting economic costs of a war increasingly defined by endurance, economists and business leaders say.
"There are signs of a crisis in the market. We don't yet know how the situation will develop," said Yevhen Shyrynos, chief editor of publisher BookChef, which lost about 800,000 books - the majority of its inventory - in a Russian attack on Kyiv on July 2.
Another 100,000 books were lost when their backup warehouse was hit in a Russian attack this week.
"It depends on Ukraine's overall economic situation," Shyrynos said.
Ukraine's economy has proved resilient during the war, adapting to blackouts, labour shortages and repeated attacks on infrastructure while remaining afloat with support from Western allies.
[[nid:1508931]]
But annual economic output, at roughly US$215 billion, remains about a fifth below its pre-invasion level.
In an effort to take the war back to Moscow, Ukraine has stepped up its own attacks on Russia's economy, targeting oil facilities and logistics warehouses as well as weapons production facilities.
Economists and executives say the conflict is becoming a test of economic endurance.
"Essentially, it's a struggle for survival – whoever can hold out the longest," said Olga Pindyuk from the Vienna Institute for International Economic Studies.
Most economists expect Ukraine's growth to slow further in 2026 as Russia intensifies strikes on infrastructure and logistics.
A survey released on Wednesday by the Kyiv-based Centre for Economic Strategy cut the median growth forecast for next year to 1.1 per cent from 2.4 per cent. Ukraine's economy grew by about 1.8 per cent in 2025.
"I meet businesses every day and there has not been such despair over losses ... since 2022," Danylo Hetmantsev, head of parliament's tax committee, told Ukrainian television.
"The economy is currently experiencing significant losses."
The defence sector is one of the few growth areas, due to the massive demand from the battlefield. About 60 per cent of state spending this year is devoted to defence.
The central bank expects the defence industry to contribute about 1.4 percentage points to Ukraine's total economic growth of 1.8 per cent this year - meaning the rest of the economy is essentially stagnant.
In particular, the vital agricultural sector - which accounts for the majority of Ukraine's exports - is struggling.
Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi has said Russian attacks on Black Sea port infrastructure could cost the farm sector between US$1.5 billion and US$3 billion this year.
Publishing faces particular challenges because books can take six to 18 months to produce.
After an early wartime boom driven by demand for Ukrainian-language titles and bans on Russian imports, publishers now face rising costs, long replacement times and repeated losses from strikes.
BookChef has looked at reducing risks for its storage facilities and expanding its network of printers. But with printing costs up about 40 per cent over the past two years, fewer Ukrainians can afford to buy books regularly.
Shyrynos expects the sector to stagnate.
"In fact, all our sectors will stagnate and decline until the war is over. The war is a vast, bottomless abyss that devours whatever funds you allocate to it."
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Study finds common plastics can biodegrade within two years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Common plastics that can persist in the environment for hundreds of years can be fully broken down by naturally occurring microbes within two years, according to a study by Malaysia's Standards and Industrial Research Institute (Sirim), Imperial College London and biotechnology firm Polymateria.
Published in a special edition of the Nature Portfolio journal Materials Degradation, the researchers described the study as a world-first, finding that plastic incorporating Polymateria's Biotransformation technology rapidly transformed into a bioavailable wax when exposed to the environment, producing no microplastics in the process.
Sirim carried out the biodegradation testing for the study, which also substantiates its national Ecolabel, SIRIM ECO 098, published in 2023 based on the UK standard BSI PAS 9017.
The wax was then fully consumed by naturally occurring microbes found in soil, leaving no traces of the original material behind.
Researchers found that polyethylene and polypropylene — the two most widely used plastic packaging materials, found in products such as cups, straws, plastic bags, films, face masks and wipes — can fully biodegrade in nature when incorporating the technology.
"Uncovering pathways through which polyolefin plastics can fully biodegrade is a remarkable discovery.
"We now know how plastic materials previously thought to be almost indestructible can safely return to nature," said Imperial College London associate professor in synthetic biology Dr Jose Jimenez Zarco, who led the microbial research, in a statement.
Sirim senior researcher Muhammad Zuhayr Dzul Haimi said the findings highlighted the importance of expanding sustainable material solutions alongside efforts to strengthen waste management systems.
"Credible alternatives such as biodegradable plastics can play an important role in supporting Malaysia's transition towards a more circular plastics economy.
"Through Sirim's Ecolabel programme, Sirim is helping to ensure that a range of credible alternatives are available for industry, policymakers and consumers to adopt with confidence," he said.
Polymateria vice president of innovations and lead author of the study Dr Florence Huynh said the research could give policymakers and industry greater confidence that scalable solutions existed for the 32 per cent of plastic packaging waste that leaked into the environment globally each year.
"It proves that common plastic materials can fully biodegrade in the open terrestrial environment.
"We're grateful to the experts at Imperial College London and Sirim for the chance to collaborate on this research," she said.
The researchers said no special conditions were required for biodegradation to occur, with microbes breaking down the material in the same way they digest natural oils or butter.
More than 300 brands across Asia, including Malaysian companies, have adopted the Biotransformation technology, joining users across about a quarter of Premier League football grounds in the United Kingdom. The technology is also being rolled out in emerging markets in Africa.
The researchers said the findings could give brands, industry and policymakers in Malaysia and across Asean greater confidence in using biodegradable plastics as part of a broader approach that also includes reducing plastic use, encouraging reuse and improving recycling.

Title: Police question KLIA staff in pilot drug probe, insider link still unclear

Title: Economic losses from natural disasters fall to US$100bil in first half of 2026: Swiss Re
Article:
ZURICH: Economic losses from natural catastrophes worldwide are estimated to have reached US$100 billion in the first half of this year, reinsurance group Swiss Re said Tuesday, a sharp decline from the period last year.
Despite severe storms in the United States and the deadly earthquakes that struck Venezuela in June, the losses were well below the US$152 billion recorded in the first half of 2025, the group said in its latest report.
The losses were also 10 per cent below the 10-year average for the period.
But Swiss Re, which serves as an insurer for insurance companies, noted that losses from natural disasters often increase in the second half of the year, mainly due to hurricanes in the North Atlantic ocean.
"A less costly first half of the year does not mean the risk has gone away," said Balz Grollimund, the group's director of Catastrophe Perils.
"One major hurricane, earthquake or wildfire can quickly change the picture."
Severe heat across Europe since June has sparked an early wildfire season in France and Spain that has already destroyed thousands of homes and businesses as well as infrastructure.
"Wildfire risk has so far accounted for only a relatively small share of insured losses in Europe. Yet it is the fastest-growing weather peril globally," the company said.
It said insured wildfire losses had risen by eight per cent to 11 per cent per year in Europe since 1970 after adjusting for inflation and other factors.
Looking forward, Swiss Re warned that the El Nino climate pattern, which began in June and is expected to peak later this year, could accentuate the cost from weather-related disasters.
"El Nino may influence tropical cyclone activity in the Central and East Pacific and could alter the risk of floods, wildfires, and other weather extremes elsewhere," it said.
"The long-term drivers of catastrophe losses remain unchanged, including growing exposure in hazard-prone areas and rising reconstruction costs," it added.

Title: [UPDATED] Only 6pct of drugs got through KLIA in first seven months - Hussein
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Drugs that slipped through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) before being intercepted overseas accounted for only about six per cent of the total drugs seized by police at the airport in the first seven months of this year.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police arrested 51 people in 41 cases at KLIA between January and July.
The operations resulted in the seizure of 1,268.16kg of drugs worth RM96.9 million.
"Cannabis accounted for the overwhelming majority of the haul, with 1,244.99kg seized, or 98.18 per cent of the total," he told reporters at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
He added that this was followed by 13.99kg of methamphetamine, or 1.10 per cent; 7.86kg of cocaine, or 0.62 per cent; and 1.32kg of ketamine, or 0.10 per cent.
"Of the 51 people arrested at KLIA, 36, or 70.6 per cent, were men, while 15, or 29.4 per cent, were women.
"The suspects came from 13 countries and territories, with British passport holders making up the largest group at 14," he said, adding that this was followed by 12 Malaysians, eight Singaporeans, five French nationals, two Indonesians, two Hong Kong passport holders, two Japanese and one each from Thailand, Ireland, Slovakia, India, Portugal and Uganda.
Hussein said separate statistics showed that 14 Malaysians were arrested overseas between January and July after travelling from KLIA with drugs.
"They comprised 11 men and three women, aged between 19 and 55.
"Six cases were recorded in Taiwan, three in Indonesia, two in the Philippines and one each in Hong Kong, Macau and the Maldives," he said, adding that those arrests involved 73.17kg of drugs worth RM5.52 million.
He said methamphetamine made up the largest portion of the drugs seized from the Malaysians overseas, at 33.53kg or 45.8 per cent.
"This was followed by 26.12kg of MDMA, or 35.7 per cent, 6.4kg of cannabis, or 8.7 per cent, 6.12kg of heroin, or 8.4 per cent, and 1kg of ketamine, or 1.4 per cent.
"If we take these two sets of statistics, what got through and was subsequently caught in other countries was about six per cent compared with what we seized or successfully prevented from being taken out.
"Six per cent. That means we are doing good at KLIA," Hussein said.
He said the figures showed that the volume of drugs intercepted at KLIA was substantially higher than the amount subsequently detected overseas among Malaysians who had departed from the airport.
Police seized about 17 times more drugs at KLIA by weight than the 73.17kg detected in the overseas cases during the same period.
The value of drugs seized at KLIA, at RM96.9 million, was also more than 17 times the RM5.52 million worth seized from the 14 Malaysians overseas.
Hussein said the statistics demonstrated the results of police enforcement efforts at the country's main international airport.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five houses damaged in Kampung Tanah Liat fire
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Five houses were damaged, including two that were extensively destroyed, in a fire along Jalan Paya, Kampung Tanah Liat, today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.32pm.
He said the fire involved two two-storey and three single-storey houses, each measuring about 50 by 60 feet.
"The first two-storey house was about 80 per cent destroyed, while the second suffered 75 per cent damage.
"For the single-storey houses, the first was about 85 per cent destroyed, while the second and third suffered damage of about 10 and five per cent respectively," he said.
The fire also damaged a Modenas motorcycle, with about 90 per cent of the vehicle destroyed.
John said three people, including an elderly man and a four-year-old girl, were safely evacuated by firefighters and were not injured.
He said 21 personnel from the Bandar Perda, Penanti, Bukit Mertajam and Jalan Perak fire and rescue stations were involved in the operation, with four fire and rescue vehicles deployed.
Firefighters subsequently carried out overhaul operations to ensure there were no remaining hazards before the operation ended at 2.58pm.
The site was subsequently handed over to the department's Fire Investigation Officer (FIO) team for further investigation.
The cause of the fire and total losses have yet to be determined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rhine water levels fall to new lows, some ship sailings halted
Article:
HAMBURG: The river Rhine in Germany has fallen to new lows in a continued heatwave, the country's inland navigation agency said on Tuesday, with cargo vessel owners often stopping sailings on southern river sections.
Inland navigation agency WSV said the navigable water depth at the chokepoint of Kaub near Koblenz was 15 cm on Tuesday, below the previous lowest recorded level of 25 cm in 2018. The river is about 1 metre deeper than the navigable depth.
"Commercial sailings through Kaub have basically stopped, it is no longer possible to book cargo shipments on the Rhine past Kaub today," one commodity trader said. "Some vessels south of Kaub face being trapped."
"There is no actual rule on when sailings at Kaub should stop because of low water, so you could see a couple of empty vessels risking it, but most sailings there have stopped," he added.
Shallow water after this summer's heatwave and scarce rainfall means cargo vessels are only able to sail 20 per cent loaded on the river, increasing costs for cargo owners. Loads must be spread among several vessels sailing part-loaded, also increasing costs.
Sailings on northern sections of the river continue, traders said.
River shippers warned on Monday that low water at Kaub threatened to stop commercial shipping this week.
Large volumes of freight are being transferred to road transport and some German authorities have relaxed weekend bans on truck driving.
Analysts said record low water on the Rhine risks curbing German economic growth, just as it is showing early signs of recovery.
Germany, like much of Europe, has experienced successive heatwaves with little rainfall this summer, leading to low water levels on waterways like the Rhine, an important shipping route for grains, minerals, coal and refined oil products.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Four NCID officers arrive in Jakarta, get two-day access to M'sian pilot
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Four Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) officers arrived in Jakarta this morning and have been granted two days to interview the Malaysian pilot arrested there.
NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said Indonesian authorities had granted the team access to the pilot tomorrow and Thursday (Aug 12 and 13).
"Four NCID officers arrived in Jakarta this morning.
"We have been given the opportunity to meet the Malaysian on Aug 12 and 13, for two days, to interview him and obtain more details," he told reporters at the Selangor police headquarters today.
Hussein said the officers would use the interviews to compare information obtained from investigations in Malaysia with the pilot's account.
They would also question him on several matters arising from information already gathered to obtain more detailed and accurate information.
"We will compare notes on what we have obtained here in terms of the syndicate and other matters, and confront him with that information so that we can get more details and more accurate information from him," he said.
Hussein said the team would also meet three Malaysian women from Kota Kinabalu who were detained in Jakarta in a separate drug case.
He said the quantity of drugs involved in their case was small and was believed to be for personal use.
The team would first assess the progress of its work in Jakarta before deciding whether to pursue further inquiries concerning another Malaysian detained in Surabaya.
"We will see what the progress is in Jakarta first and decide later," he said.
It was reported that the 39-year-old suspect flew on Malaysia Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta before he was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport on July 28 with
70,000 ecstasy pills
.
He was also tested positive for three types of drugs, meth, MDMA and cocaine, after he landed in Jakarta.
During preliminary investigations, the suspect admitted he was instructed by an individual to transport the drugs to Jakarta in exchange for RM50,000.
The suspect told investigators that upon arriving in Jakarta, he would be directed by someone believed to be based in Malaysia that another person would collect the items at a hotel or accommodation.
The suspect also told investigators that he had acted as a drug courier three times.
It had also been reported that Bukit Aman would dispatch a
team of investigators and intelligence officers
to Jakarta, Indonesia, from Aug 11 to 15 as part of its probe into the case.
The team would work with Indonesian authorities to gather further information on the syndicate believed to be behind the operation, including identifying the source of the drugs, the smuggling methods used, and any links between the suspect and syndicates operating in Indonesia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'KLIA too hot': International drug syndicates turning to other airports
Article:
SHAH ALAM: International drug syndicates are believed to be turning to other airports as intensified enforcement makes the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) increasingly difficult for them to exploit.
This shift was observed during Op Lejogaster, where police uncovered an international syndicate which planned to move cannabis buds out of the country through Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas.
Police seized RM21.62 million worth of cannabis buds through this latest operations. The drugs were bound for Europe.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said syndicates were constantly searching for alternative routes and weaknesses in enforcement.
"When KLIA becomes 'hot', they may use other airports.
"As I have always said, these syndicates are constantly looking for openings and will use whatever avenues are available to them, whether by land, sea or air," he told reporters at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
Hussein said investigations under Op Lejogaster showed how the syndicate had made use of locations near airports as part of its trafficking operation.
"The syndicate obtained cannabis buds from a neighbouring country before bringing them into Malaysia through the northern part of the peninsula.
"The drugs were then stored temporarily at houses near airports, including around Bayan Lepas in Penang, before being handed over to drug mules for transportation overseas," he said adding that some consignments were kept in Penang while others were brought to the Klang Valley.
He said the market for cannabis buds at present is Europe.
"Investigations found that the syndicate used routes through Penang International Airport and KLIA, with some flights travelling directly while others transited in Singapore.
"London was among the main destinations, where another syndicate would receive the consignments before they were moved elsewhere in Europe.
"Op Lejogaster, conducted between July 12 and Aug 3 following intelligence gathering and surveillance, resulted in nine people being arrested and drugs and assets worth RM21.73 million seized," he said adding that the nine suspects comprised one Malaysian and eight foreign men aged between 22 and 51.
He said of the foreigners, five were carrying Portuguese passports, two were Singaporeans and one was a Myanmar national.
Hussein said the group was headed by a Portuguese national who coordinated its activities from Europe.
"The syndicate's drug mules did not necessarily know one another and were placed in separate hotels while awaiting instructions.
"They would wait until the syndicate told them their luggage was ready and informed them of their destination," he said.
Police seized 270.27kg of cannabis buds worth about RM21.62 million during the operation.
Assets worth RM117,172 were also seized, bringing the total value of seizures to RM21.73 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor Baru-Singapore RTS LINK set to lift JB property demand, but Malaysians may drive growth
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to lift property demand in central Johor Baru, particularly around Bukit Chagar.
But the growth could be driven as much by Malaysians working in Singapore as by Singaporean buyers and tenants, an analyst said.
JS-SEZ Monitor founder Nasser Ismail told Business Times the RTS would make living in Johor Baru while working in Singapore more practical by offering a faster and more predictable daily commute.
"The RTS is likely to increase demand for homes in central Johor Baru, especially around Bukit Chagar. But I would not see this simply as Singaporeans coming over to buy property.
"A large part of the demand could come from Malaysians who work in Singapore but want to live in JB," he said.
The RTS Link, scheduled to begin operations on Jan 1 next year, will connect Bukit Chagar with Woodlands North in Singapore, potentially making cross-border commuting less dependent on the Causeway.
Nasser said a Singapore study estimated the RTS could generate an additional 11.2 million Singapore-to-Johor round trips annually, along with more than S$1.05 billion (RM3.35 billion) in additional annual spending in Johor.
"If the RTS makes the daily journey faster and more predictable, that will make living, eating, shopping and doing business in JB much more attractive," he said.
The impact could extend beyond condominium demand, with strategically located residential properties increasingly being valued for their potential commercial use, he added.
"Houses in the right parts of central JB are increasingly being looked at not just as homes, but as possible cafés, restaurants, clinics, offices or other businesses."
Nasser cited a recent Taman Melodies rental listing of a property at RM18,000 a month, compared with RM7,000 in 2023, as an example of how landlords were beginning to price in commercial potential.
"It is only one example, but it shows how landlords are beginning to price in the commercial potential of well-located residential properties," he said.
He said stronger Singaporean spending in Johor could also attract more Singapore businesses, further increasing competition for strategically located properties.
"That would be positive for owners, but it is also a double-edged sword because local residents and smaller businesses could eventually find themselves priced out of parts of the city," he said.
However, Nasser said the RTS property premium would depend largely on connectivity beyond Bukit Chagar.
"Accessibility is what creates the property premium. If passengers can move easily from the RTS into the wider city centre through good walkways, feeder buses and public transport, the impact can spread to many more neighbourhoods.
"If the journey becomes difficult again once people leave the station, most of the benefit will remain concentrated within a relatively small area around Bukit Chagar," he said.
He said the RTS property story was therefore bigger than rising condominium prices around the station.
"It is about how improved access to Singapore changes the value of central JB. The better we connect Bukit Chagar to the rest of the city, the wider the benefits will spread," he said.
Howver, Nasser cautioned that rapidly rising property prices and rents could eventually squeeze local residents and small businesses if they outpaced incomes.
The RTS and Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) are expected to reinforce each other by improving connectivity while attracting investment, jobs and cross-border spending.
However, rising demand will have to be matched against the growing supply of high-rise residential projects around the RTS and Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) corridor.
The key question is whether genuine demand will absorb the new units or whether the rush to capitalise on the RTS could create pockets of oversupply.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hong Kong deepens Malaysia's and Asean trade ties with a new Kuala Lumpur office
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Kong is stepping up economic and trade ties with Malaysia and the wider Asean region through a newly established Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office (HKETO) in Kuala Lumpur.
Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Commerce and Economic Development secretary Algernon Yau said the office would strengthen government-to-government and business-to-business links.
He said it would also facilitate two-way trade and investment across finance and fintech, innovation and technology, professional services, the green economy, logistics and creative industries.
"Malaysia is our eighth largest partner. Together with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, Invest Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Tourism Board, the Kuala Lumpur ETO will steer ahead," he said.
The office, which began operations in December 2025, was established with strong support and swift approval from the Malaysian government.
Yau said Kuala Lumpur was strategically positioned to deepen Hong Kong's engagement with Malaysia, Brunei, Laos and Pakistan.
He said Malaysia and Hong Kong could collaborate on economic transformation, particularly education, technology and artificial intelligence, alongside Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis development.
"People-to-people ties are more important than everything. Once you establish the friendship, you build the trust, and then we can do everything together," he said.
The Kuala Lumpur office is Hong Kong's 15th overseas economic and trade office globally and its fourth in ASEAN, following Singapore, Jakarta and Bangkok.
Asean is Hong Kong's second-largest trading partner in goods, with trade growing at an average annual rate of 7.6 per cent between 2021 and 2025.
It is also Hong Kong's third-largest services trading partner, while Hong Kong handled HK$680.5 billion in re-exports between mainland China and ASEAN in 2025.
The figure represented eight per cent of total bilateral trade between mainland China and ASEAN, underscoring Hong Kong's role as a key regional entrepot.
"Asean country is the second biggest trade partner, with Hong Kong and Malaysia taking a very strong position. I think it's the fourth strongest trading partner with Hong Kong as well.
"In many different trading areas, including normal merchandise trade and professional services, for example, now it's developing on the innovation and technology.
"E-commerce, for example, is very strong in Malaysia as well, and Hong Kong is building on e-commerce and digital trade. All these are the cooperation areas between the two economies, now and for the longer term future," Yau said.
Officiating the opening, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the office's establishment was timely following 10 memorandums of understanding signed during the "Think Business, Think Hong Kong" campaign.
He said Malaysia also expected stronger capital market cooperation following an agreement between the Securities Commission Malaysia and Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission.
The agreement covers mutual recognition and cross-listing of covered funds, particularly exchange-traded funds and real estate investment funds.
"This is the opportunity that we hope to collaborate with Hong Kong even more. We hope to tap into your financial market. We hope to tap into your service industry. Your expertise to help us move up the value chain," said Loke.
Loke said Malaysia's growth strategy covered Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Bahru, the east coast, Sabah and Sarawak, creating opportunities for broader cooperation with Hong Kong.
He said potential areas included semiconductors, electronics, artificial intelligence, the digital economy and manufacturing, alongside creative industries such as film production.
"We hope to see more direct flights between Malaysia and Hong Kong, including to Kota Kinabalu, Kuching, Johor Bahru, Langkawi and even Ipoh. We believe that stronger connectivity will help people, businesses and communities in both economies move more easily and strengthen our ties," added Loke.

Title: Ebola deaths surpass 2,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo
Article:
DAKAR: Democratic Republic of Congo said on Tuesday that confirmed Ebola deaths had reached 2,011, the latest grim milestone in what health officials have described as the fastest-spreading outbreak on record.
The latest data from Congo's public health institute, seen by Reuters, also reported 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces.
Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have helped the virus spread more rapidly than in previous outbreaks.
The current outbreak, Congo's 17th, is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments.
The World Health Organisation has declared the outbreak, which has also led to cases in neighbouring Uganda, a public health emergency of international concern.
A study published last month in the journal Science found that transmission may have begun in January or earlier in Ituri province, identifying more than 500 suspected cases between mid-January and May 15.
Shortages of medical supplies and insecurity in affected areas have complicated efforts to trace contacts, isolate patients and curb transmission.
The Congolese government data shows that only West Africa's 2014 to 2016 Ebola outbreak was bigger, with 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths recorded across ​Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone, according to the WHO.
It took nearly five months from the declaration of that outbreak to hit 1,000 deaths, whereas Congo's current outbreak has hit 2,000 deaths in less than three months.
In an Ebola outbreak in Congo from  2018 to 2020, it took a little over 12 months to hit 2,000 deaths.
In the current outbreak, deaths have jumped from 1,000 to 2,000 in less than a month, further underscoring how quickly the virus is spreading.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israeli soldiers, settlers use grenades and physical assaults against Palestinian journalists
Article:
RAMALLAH: The Palestinian Journalists Syndicate said it documented 108 attacks and other violations against Palestinian journalists and media workers by Israeli occupation forces and settlers during July, Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported.
In its monthly report, the syndicate's Freedoms Committee said the violations included detentions, interrogations, physical assaults, obstruction of media coverage, raids and attacks involving tear gas and stun grenades.
Brief detentions and restrictions on reporting accounted for 58 documented incidents, making them the most common violations during the month.
The committee also recorded 11 attacks by Israeli settlers against journalists and media crews in the West Bank.
These reportedly involved physical assaults, threats and attempts to prevent journalists from covering events.
Israeli occupation forces used tear gas and stun grenades against journalists in 12 cases, the report said, causing some reporters to suffer breathing difficulties.
Six beatings and four incidents in which journalists sustained bleeding injuries were also documented, including injuries from missile and artillery shrapnel in the Gaza Strip.
The committee reported the detention of two journalists and the interrogation of four others over their professional activities.
Four raids on journalists' homes and media organisations were also recorded, including the closure of one media outlet and the seizure of its contents.
Three cases involved the seizure or destruction of journalistic equipment, while footage was deleted in two other incidents.
Two journalists were expelled from al-Aqsa Mosque and prohibited from entering its courtyards for specified periods, according to the report.
The syndicate said the figures demonstrated the range of dangers facing Palestinian journalists and called for their protection, respect for press freedom and accountability for attacks on media workers.
TAGS: Palestinian, journalists, Israel, detention, assaults, raid
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's low costs, talent draw investors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's competitive labour costs, low land prices and strong human resources have made the country investor-friendly, said Hong Kong-listed Far East Consortium International Ltd.
Its chairman and chief executive officer Tan Sri David Chiu said Malaysia's cultural similarities with Hong Kong also make it easier for Malaysian professionals to manage businesses and operations there.
"If you have a team in Malaysia (and) you want to send them to Hong Kong to run your business there, it is not at all difficult because of the similar culture (between Malaysia and Hong Kong)," he said during a plenary session at the Think Business, Think Hong Kong symposium here today.
Besides that, Chiu said, the highly supportive local government community towards foreign investors has also helped his company to grow further over three decades.
"We have an annual turnover of over RM3 billion a year. It all happened because Malaysians are very friendly to foreign investors," he said.
Today's symposium marked the Hong Kong Trade Development Council's (HKTDC) flagship overseas promotion in Kuala Lumpur, offering Malaysian business leaders direct access to government officials, investors, founders, innovators and professional service providers.
In a statement, the HKTDC said the one-day event brought together business leaders from Hong Kong and Malaysia for a day of dialogue, networking, business matching and one-on-one consultations.
"Among them are over 200 government and business leaders, start-up entrepreneurs and professional service providers from Hong Kong, marking a historic high," it added.

Title: Pas deputy president Tuan Ibrahim leaves Anwar defamation suit to lawyers
Article:
KOTA BARU: PAS deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he had left the matter concerning the defamation suit filed against him by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to his lawyers.
He said the remarks he made were general in nature and had also been raised by various parties and sources.
"I have handed the matter over to my lawyers to take the necessary action.
"What I stated was something general, which has also been mentioned by many parties and from various sources," said the Kubang Kerian Member of Parliament.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has filed a defamation suit against Tuan Ibrahim over remarks allegedly made during a political speech in June.
Anwar's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said the suit was filed at the High Court on Monday.
Sankara said the proceedings arose from statements allegedly made by the defendant during a political speech at Felda Jenderak Utara, Kuala Krau, Pahang, on or around June 14, 2026, which were false and defamatory of his client.
The suit also relates to the publication and republication of the allegedly defamatory statements in video recordings and on social media platforms, including YouTube and Facebook, as well as on the defendant's Facebook account, "@Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man".
Anwar's claim is based on alleged slander and libel.

Title: Man appealing for shorter sentence gets maximum 30 years for baby daughter's death
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A man who appealed for a shorter jail term for causing his 2-month-old daughter's death had his sentence increased to 30 years by the Court of Appeal today.
Justice Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, who delivered the decision of a three-member bench, said the court had discretionary power under Section 60 of the Courts of Judicature Act 1964 to enhance the sentence despite the lack of a prosecution cross-appeal.
Also on the bench were Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah and K. Muniandy.
Hayatul said the 16-year prison sentence imposed by the Shah Alam High Court did not reflect the seriousness of the offence and the violence involved.
The court set aside the 16-year sentence and substituted it with the maximum 30-year sentence under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, ordered to run from his arrest on Aug 1, 2022.
She said the court considered that the deceased was a helpless infant dependent on her parents for protection.
"Unfortunately, in the present case, the infant was instead subjected to abuse. It was not a one-off incident but rather repeated inhumane acts," she said.
She said that on July 30, 2022, the infant's mother heard her crying in the living room, where the appellant was present.
Hayatul said the appellant took the infant from a cushion on the floor and slammed her down, causing her to cry. The following day, he yanked her hand, pressed her stomach, and slammed her onto the cushion again, causing her head to hit the corner of a table.
She said a post-mortem report confirmed the infant died from blunt trauma to the head.
Hayatul said the appellant's argument that the High Court failed to consider his young age did not align with the violent nature of his conduct.
She said the 30-year sentence would give the appellant time to reflect on his cruel actions, reform, and serve as a warning to society.
Earlier, Daniel, through counsel K.A. Ramu, appealed for a shorter sentence, asking the court to consider that he was 21 at the time of the offence.
He said Daniel, 25, was initially charged with murder, but the prosecution accepted a representation to reduce the charge under Section 304(a) of the Penal Code, to which he pleaded guilty.
Deputy public prosecutor P. Sarulatha told the court that although there was no cross-appeal by the prosecution, the court could still increase the sentence under Section 60 of the Act.
The Shah Alam High Court in May sentenced Daniel to 16 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of his infant daughter at his home in Bandar Tasik Puteri, Rawang, between July 30 and 31, 2022.
He has one final avenue of appeal with the Federal Court.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM8.49mil drug haul seized from apartment in Masai, two arrested
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police busted a drug distribution syndicate after seizing 96.76kg of various drugs worth RM8.49 million from an apartment in Persiaran Senibong, Masai, which had allegedly been rented as a storage facility.
Also arrested were two men aged 30 and 39.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the raid on Aug 5 led to the arrest of the two men suspected to be involved in the syndicate.
He said the operation was mounted following intelligence gathered, with two raids carried out in the Bandar Seri Alam area at 10.30am.
"The first raid at the apartment led to the arrest of the 30-year-old man who acted as the storekeeper.
"Checks uncovered 132,600 Ermin 5 pills, 53,000 ecstasy pills, 290 packets of suspected ecstasy powder, 13 packets of suspected ketamine and packets of suspected MDMA powder," he told a press conference at the Johor police headquarters here today.
The second raid was conducted at a terrace house in Taman Ehsan Jaya, where police arrested the other suspect, who allegedly assisted the syndicate mastermind and was responsible for paying the storekeeper's salary.
No drugs were found at the second premises.
Rahaman said the syndicate was believed to been active since early May and had targeted the local market, particularly patrons of entertainment centres.
"The drugs seized could have been abused by an estimated 392,098 people," he said.
Police also seized a Honda City, Toyota Vellfire, BMW, Proton Saga, a motorcycle and RM100,000 during the operation.
Rahaman said the syndicate's modus operandi was to use gated and guarded apartment units as drug storage facilities before distributing the drugs to the local market.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment for life and whipping upon conviction.
Initial urine screening found both suspects negative for drugs, while checks showed they had previous criminal records.
"Both suspects have been remanded for seven days from Aug 6 until tomorrow.
"Police are tracking down the syndicate mastermind," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Human oversight must remain central as newsrooms embrace AI
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Artificial intelligence (AI) can make newsrooms more productive, but it cannot replace the editorial judgement and accountability that underpin credible journalism, media practitioners said.
Former Media Prima Bhd news and editorial operations executive director and New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd chief executive officer Mustapha Kamil said the extent to which AI would reshape journalism remains an open question.
"If you ask me, will it take over entirely the presence of the newsroom? Maybe not, or not yet, or maybe this machine has never been taught how to do so.
"But in the final analysis, there must always be human oversight in the operation of the newsroom," he said.
Mustapha, who was also formerly Business Times managing editor, was speaking at a panel session titled "Credibility in the Age of AI: Navigating the New Frontier" at a lunch escape programme organised by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) in collaboration with the Malaysian Press Institute (MPI).
The panel also featured RTM director-general Ashwad Ismail, Free Malaysia Today managing director Azeem Abu Bakar and Petronas senior general manager of strategic communications Datin Arni Laily Anwarrudin.
The session was moderated by Petronas general manager of upstream strategic communications Kitt Othman.
Azeem said the use of AI did not in itself undermine credibility as long as journalists remained accountable for the accuracy of their work.
"AI is a tool. No matter how you do your work, whether you're in the media, other industries or corporate communications, when you submit your work to your boss or put it out for the public to see, you have to check that it is accurate.
"If it is accurate, then it should be fine. AI is simply a more powerful tool today," he said.
Azeem said credibility becomes an issue when users rely on AI without knowing how to use it effectively or having sufficient knowledge of the subject they are working on.
Simply prompting AI to generate content without understanding the subject, he said, could leave users unable to recognise inaccuracies or errors in its output.
"If you know the subject matter really well, you can spot those errors and correct them, while having AI do the heavy lifting.
"At the end of the day, AI is a reflection of your expertise," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US$620mil returned to sender, not Najib's account, court hears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The US$620 million returned by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to its sender in 2013 was not transferred back into his bank account, the High Court heard today.
Offshore asset recovery expert Angela Barkhouse, the third witness for 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), agreed with Najib's lawyer Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah that the money was returned to Tanore Finance Corp, which he identified as the sender.
Barkhouse, who is also managing director of Kroll (Cayman) Ltd and head of Kroll's Offshore Practice, was asked whether the money was returned after the 13th General Election (GE13) in 2013.
However, she said she could not confirm when the funds were returned.
Shafee then suggested that his client had returned US620 million of the US681 million "donation" because he had not used the money and felt uncomfortable keeping such a large amount in his account.
According to the senior lawyer, the money was returned to Tanore after GE13 in 2013 on the understanding that it was an Arab donation.
Asked whether she knew why Najib returned the US$620 million, Barkhouse said: "I do not know."
Shafee: "Have you ever wondered why someone who received US$681 million would return most of it to the sender?"
Barkhouse: "That is a fair question."
However, Barkhouse said this version of the return of the funds was inconsistent with bank documents she had examined and the witness statement of international financial investigator Richard Templeman.
She said Richard's investigation showed that the instruction to return the money was given by Low Taek Jho's associate, Eric Tan.
She said Templeman's witness statement indicated that the instruction to return the funds was made by Tan and was related to SRC International.
Shafee, however, said this was the first time he had heard of the matter and described it as making no sense.
Barkhouse was testifying in the civil suit filed by 1MDB and four of its subsidiaries against Najib and six others over the alleged misappropriation of US$5.6 billion belonging to the company.
In the suit, 1MDB and its subsidiaries — 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited — are the plaintiffs.
The suit was filed on May 7, 2021, naming Najib, former 1MDB finance director Terrence Geh, former executive director Casey Tang, former chief investment officer Vincent Beng, former chief operating officer Radhi Mohamad, former investment director Kelvin Tan and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil as defendants.
According to the writ of summons, the plaintiffs alleged, among other things, that the defendants had committed breaches of trust, breached statutory duties, abused their powers and conspired to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus resumes tomorrow.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pahang Pas: Door open to Umno cooperation, or election clash
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang Pas is open to political cooperation with Umno under the 'penyatuan ummah' (Muslim unity) concept ahead of the 16th General Election.
However, the party is also prepared to face its former allies at the polls if talks fail to materialise.
Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said no discussions had been held with Barisan Nasional or Umno so far, but the party was ready to sit down for talks.
"Amid the current political scenario, and taking into account what happened in Johor and Negri Sembilan, Pas calls on political parties, including Umno, to work together in the name of strengthening unity among the Muslim community," he said when contacted.
Rosli said Pahang Pas was prepared to initiate discussions if an opportunity arose, in line with calls by party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang for greater political cooperation under the Muslim unity concept.
"We agree that unity of the ummah should be pursued. If Umno agrees, we will welcome it with open arms...Pas is always ready," he said.
He was asked to elaborate on his Facebook post yesterday, in which he wrote: "Our primary choice is the unity of the ummah, but if they choose to clash, we are fully prepared for it."
Last week,
Pahang Pas deputy commissioner Datuk Andansura Rabu said
the ongoing Perikatan Nasional Jelajah Teraju Pahang campaign, led by Pas, would proceed as scheduled.
Pahang Pas and Umno established ties under the Muafakat Nasional pact in 2019, when Pakatan Harapan was in power at the federal level. However, the cooperation ended the following year after Pas joined Bersatu to form PN.

Title: No enemies, debts: Family suspects mistaken identity in Kepong attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The family of a woman who suffered burns to about 50 per cent of her body after being doused with fuel and set alight at a four-digit gaming outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong believes the suspect may have mistaken her for his intended target.
The victim's daughter, Joyce Yap, said the family had no known enemies or outstanding debts and could not understand why her mother was targeted.
"We have never had problems or debts with anyone, so we are puzzled and do not understand why our mother was subjected to such a cruel act," she said.
The incident occurred on Sunday when the woman, in her 60s, was working alone at the outlet. The premises usually also employed part-time workers on weekends.
Yap said the absence of any previous threats or disputes led the family to suspect the attacker may have mistaken her mother for someone else.
"Only my mother was working that Sunday, although part-time workers sometimes work on that day.
"That is why our family has no clue about the suspect's motive or why he would do this to our mother," she said.
She said her mother remained in critical condition and was receiving intensive care in the intensive care unit of a hospital.
Meanwhile, Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng's special assistant, Dic Lai, said the victim's condition remained unstable due to the severity of her burns.
He said Lim had offered a RM5,000 reward yesterday for credible information, but no new leads had been received as of noon today.
"As far as I know, officers from the Kuala Lumpur serious crimes division (D9) have taken over the case and are actively working to identify and track down the suspect," he said.
Police have urged anyone with information to come forward to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muhyiddin calls for Tabung Haji forensic audit to be completed within a year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin has called on the government to complete a comprehensive and independent forensic audit of Tabung Haji's management within a year.
Following the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrim fund, he said the audit was needed to trace the flow of funds and identify elements of fraud, abuse of power and negligence.
"Given the complex governance weaknesses and leakages in Tabung Haji's fund management, a comprehensive and continuous forensic audit must be carried out immediately and completed within one year.
"Anyone responsible for causing losses to Tabung Haji's funds, whether through fraud, abuse of power or negligence, must be brought to justice," Muhyiddin said while debating the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat today.
The 211-page RCI report revealed governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in the fair value of investments.
It also found that Tabung Haji should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the reported RM3.4 billion profit, had Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards been fully applied.
Muhyiddin said the RCI's finding that Tabung Haji suffered estimated cumulative losses of between RM10 billion and RM12.6 billion from 2014 to 2020 warranted serious attention and firm action without compromise.
The Pagoh member of Parliament said critical investment decisions involving billions of ringgit had been made without proper risk assessment, exposing depositors' funds to significant risks.
"The losses were covered up through creative accounting, while the government at the time insisted that Tabung Haji remained profitable even though the RCI report showed it had actually suffered billions of ringgit in losses," he said.
Muhyiddin said the episode raised serious questions over governance and accountability.
"How could negligence, or rather, the falsification of Tabung Haji's financial reports, be allowed to happen?
"This must never be allowed to recur, and those involved must face stern action," he said.
He added that restoring public confidence in Tabung Haji required the government to fully implement the RCI's recommendations, act on the findings of the proposed forensic audit and strengthen governance to safeguard depositors' funds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MP: TH leadership sackings in 2021 must be explained
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The decision to abruptly terminate the contracts of Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) chief executive officer and chairman in 2021 must be explained, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Syerleena Abdul Rashid (PH-Bukit Bendera) said the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) found that the move had affected the institution's reform process.
Syerleena said the RCI found that TH chief executive officer Datuk Nik Mohd Hasyudeen Yusoff and chairman Tan Sri Md Nor Md Yusof had delivered and were working to improve the institution before their contracts were terminated.
Nik Mohd Hasyudeen was terminated on May 5, 2021, several months before his contract was due to expire on Aug 31 that year, while Md Nor was terminated on Oct 15, 2021, despite having had his contract renewed for two years from July 20, 2020.
"I want to stress that this is not a DAP allegation. This is a finding of the RCI," she said during a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat to debate the RCI report on TH today.
Syerleena questioned why the two senior officials were removed while they were implementing improvements at the Islamic savings and pilgrimage institution.
"Why were the people who were fixing Tabung Haji terminated? Who made that decision? What performance assessment was used? Was the decision made in the interest of the institution or were there other considerations?" she asked.
She said TH's management and leadership should not change direction whenever there was a change in government, stressing that the institution should not be subject to political cycles.
"Tabung Haji is not a place for leadership changes according to political seasons."
She said the RCI had completed its task by examining TH's governance, financial crisis, restructuring and other related matters, and that the government and enforcement agencies must now act on its findings.
"If there are those who have breached the law, investigate and charge them.
"If there are those who abused their power, hold them accountable."
Syerleena also called for those who had received warnings but deliberately failed to act to be identified, as well as for any political decisions that disrupted TH's recovery process to be disclosed to Parliament.
She said the RCI report should not become merely a document debated in Parliament before being put aside and forgotten.
"What the people see now is very bad: warnings were given but ignored, billions of ringgit were affected but no one was held responsible, reports were prepared but not used, and those who tried to fix the situation were terminated."
Syerleena also rejected any attempt to attribute the origins of TH's financial crisis to the Pakatan Harapan administration, saying the problems had already persisted for years when the coalition took over the federal government in 2018.
She said the PH administration had instead initiated efforts to assess and address TH's financial position, including appointing PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) to review its accounts and implementing a recovery and restructuring plan.
The Dewan Rakyat convened for a one-day special sitting to discuss the RCI report, with proceedings beginning at 10am with Zulkifli's briefing, followed by a question-and-debate session involving MPs.
The 211-page RCI report revealed governance weaknesses, including political interference in management and the distribution of profits without adequately accounting for depreciation and declines in investment fair value.
It also found that TH should have recorded a net loss of RM1.4 billion in 2017, instead of the reported RM3.4 billion profit, had Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) been fully applied.

Title: Dogs top animal abuse, neglect cases in Malaysia, says group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dogs are the most commonly abused and neglected animals in Malaysia, with uncontrolled breeding and perceptions that they pose a safety threat contributing to the problem.
Malaysian Animal Association president Associate Professor Arie Dwi Andika said records obtained from authorities showed dogs accounted for the highest number of reported cases, followed by cats, horses and cattle.
"Many dogs are abused, beaten and poisoned. Some are abandoned by their owners, left without proper care or food, or kept on excessively short chains. Cats face similar problems," he said when contacted today.
Arie said complaints involving neglected horses had also increased, with some found without proper shelter and requiring rescue.
Cattle were also frequently neglected, he said, with some breeders allowing them to roam in search of food.
According to Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) records, 4,133 complaints involving animal abuse, neglect and welfare were recorded in 2024.
"About half of these involved dogs, followed by cats. In 2023, 38,833 complaints involving dogs, including nuisance cases reported to local authorities, were recorded," he said.
Arie said on average, an estimated 2,000 dogs were caught each year by each of the country's 156 local authorities, with most being strays or abandoned by their owners.
He attributed the high number of abuse and neglect cases involving dogs to their growing population and the perception that they pose a threat to public safety.
"In terms of population, the number of dogs appears to exceed the number of responsible owners, resulting in many being left to fend for themselves.
"This creates conflict with communities, where dogs are often perceived as a safety threat," he said.
Arie said some irresponsible owners also failed to understand their responsibilities towards the welfare of their pets and the impact on public safety.
He said the association had no objection to authorities taking action against dogs allowed to roam freely if they posed a risk of injury or accidents.
He said perceptions that dogs were dangerous, noisy or dirty also contributed to negative attitudes towards them.
Some dogs were also kept by factories and construction companies as guard dogs but abandoned once their services were no longer needed, he said.
"When these dogs are no longer needed as guard dogs and are not neutered, their population can grow uncontrollably," he said.
Arie urged all stakeholders to strengthen animal ownership and management practices through greater awareness and education.S
"People need to understand that keeping a living creature comes with responsibility and requires proper food, shelter, hygiene and care.
"Pet owners must be responsible and treat animal ownership as a trust. If they cannot meet these needs, it is better not to keep animals and to find another hobby," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Civil society groups, PKR members demand action on TH RCI findings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A coalition of civil society groups and PKR members has submitted two memorandums to the government calling for immediate, impartial and transparent action on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) operations from 2014 to 2020.
The group gathered outside Parliament today and handed over the memorandums to representatives from the Prime Minister's Office and the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs).
The first memorandum, addressed to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, outlined six demands focused on accountability, governance reform and transparency.
Among them was a call for an independent forensic audit of 14 investments identified in the RCI report for further scrutiny, including their approval processes, risk assessments, transactions, potential conflicts of interest and parties responsible.
The coalition also called for the audit findings to be referred to relevant enforcement agencies and, where legally permissible, disclosed to Parliament and the public.
It also urged amendments to the Tabung Haji Act to bar active politicians from serving on the board and require appointments based on qualifications, expertise, integrity and professional independence rather than political considerations.
The memorandum also called for an authoritative religious ruling on the zakat status of depositors' savings during the period examined by the RCI, including the calculation method, amount that should have been paid, amount actually paid and party responsible for its fulfilment.
The second memorandum, addressed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, called for the RCI findings to be assessed from the perspective of Islamic law and maqasid syariah, given TH's role in managing the savings of millions of Muslims seeking to perform the haj.
It also called for a monitoring mechanism under the Religious Affairs portfolio to ensure syariah and Islamic governance considerations were incorporated into TH's reform process.
"TH is not merely a financial institution. Within it lie the efforts, sacrifices, prayers and hopes of millions of Muslims who wish to become guests of Allah in the Holy Land," the memorandum said.
The memorandums were submitted as the Dewan Rakyat held a special sitting today to discuss the RCI report.
Zulkifli began proceedings with an
explanation of the report
, but the sitting was disrupted when opposition MPs staged a walkout after their request to postpone the sitting over Anwar's absence was rejected.
Anwar later
apologised
for missing the sitting, saying he was recovering under medical care.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Are e-wallets better than cards and cash in Malaysia?
Article:
E-WALLETS are often more convenient than cards or cash for everyday payments in Malaysia, particularly at hawker stalls, cafés, convenience stores and small retailers.
For tourists, cards are often the principal payment method at hotels because they may also be needed for deposits, pre-authorisations and online reservations, while cash is still required at some markets and in rural areas.
Popular e-wallets in Malaysia include Touch 'n Go eWallet, GrabPay, Boost, ShopeePay and Setel. Consumers can also make QR payments through banking applications such as MAE by Maybank and CIMB OCTO.
Many of these services support DuitNow QR, Malaysia's national QR payment standard. It allows participating banking and e-wallet applications to make payments through a single merchant QR code, rather than requiring separate codes for each provider.
Payment method
Best suited to
Main limitation
E-wallet or banking app
Small shops, food stalls and everyday spending
Requires a supported account, charged phone and connectivity
Debit or credit card
Hotels, major retailers and larger purchases
Not accepted by every microbusiness

Markets, rural areas and payment emergencies
Less convenient and difficult to recover if lost
For most people, e-wallets are not a complete replacement for cards and cash. The most reliable arrangement is to have a digital payment option, a physical card and a small cash reserve.
IS MALAYSIA CASHLESS, OR DO TOURISTS STILL NEED CASH?
Malaysia is increasingly cashless, especially in Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Johor Baru and other major urban centres.
Cards and QR payments are commonly accepted at shopping centres, hotels, chain restaurants, pharmacies and tourist attractions.
Tourists should nevertheless carry some Malaysian ringgit. Cash may still be required at traditional markets, older food stalls, rural businesses and smaller transport or parking facilities.
It also provides a useful backup when a card terminal is unavailable, a mobile connection fails or a foreign card is rejected.
Visitors do not necessarily need to download a Malaysian e-wallet. International Visa and Mastercard cards are widely accepted, although acceptance varies and foreign transaction charges may apply.
WHY DO SMALL SHOPS PREFER QR OVER CARD TERMINALS?
Small shops often prefer QR payments because they are easier and less expensive to introduce than conventional card terminals.
A merchant can display a printed DuitNow QR code and receive payments from participating banks and e-wallets without operating separate hardware for every provider.
The system helps businesses reduce costs, track sales and reconcile payments through consolidated records. This is particularly practical for hawkers, pasar malam traders, home-based sellers and independent cafés.
GrabPay, for example, states that its users can scan participating DuitNow QR codes through the Grab application.
QR payments can still create difficulties when internet coverage is weak.
ARE E-WALLETS SAFE TO USE IN MALAYSIA?
E-wallets are generally safe when users choose legitimate providers and apply basic account security measures.
Bank Negara Malaysia's electronic money requirements cover areas including fraud controls, phishing, system security and customer protection. Individual providers may also use PINs, biometric logins and multi-factor authentication to protect accounts.
The more common danger is social engineering. A scammer may impersonate a bank, merchant, government agency or delivery company and persuade the victim to reveal a one-time password, approve a transfer or install an unknown application.
Users should check the merchant name and payment amount before authorising a transaction.
They should never disclose verification codes, approve unexpected requests or access an e-wallet through links sent in unsolicited messages.
Keeping only a reasonable spending balance in an e-wallet can also limit potential losses. A stolen phone should be reported immediately to the wallet provider and mobile network operator.
CAN INTERNATIONAL TOURISTS USE DIGITAL WALLETS IN MALAYSIA?
Some international tourists can use supported home-country wallets to pay at participating DuitNow QR merchants in Malaysia.
PayNet's cross-border QR network connects selected payment applications from countries and territories including Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Cambodia.
Supported visitors can scan an eligible DuitNow QR code, confirm the amount in their application and pay without opening a Malaysian bank account.
Travellers using participating Alipay+ applications may also pay at enabled Malaysian merchants.
PayNet said in March 2025 that travellers using participating Alipay+ applications from 10 countries and regions could pay at more than 2.5 million DuitNow QR touchpoints.
In February 2026, PayNet separately reported that Malaysia had more than 2.9 million DuitNow QR merchants.
Availability depends on the visitor's country, bank, wallet provider and the merchant's QR arrangement.
Indian travellers are also expected to gain access through supported UPI applications under a cross-border agreement announced by PayNet and NPCI International in February 2026.
Tourists should check their wallet's overseas payment settings before travelling.
A physical card and some ringgit remain advisable because not every foreign wallet works at every DuitNow QR location.
MORE FAQS ABOUT E-WALLETS IN MALAYSIA
How do QR e-wallet payments work in Malaysia?
Open a supported e-wallet or banking application, scan the merchant's DuitNow QR code and check the merchant name and amount.
Authorise the payment using a PIN, fingerprint or facial recognition, then wait for confirmation.
Which e-wallets are commonly used in Malaysia?
Common examples include Touch 'n Go eWallet, GrabPay, Boost, ShopeePay and Setel.
Touch 'n Go eWallet and GrabPay both support a range of everyday purchases, while participating applications can also scan DuitNow QR codes.
Is DuitNow QR an e-wallet?
No. DuitNow QR is a national payment standard operated by PayNet. It connects participating banks, e-wallets and merchants through a common QR code.
Should tourists use an e-wallet, card or cash in Malaysia?
Cards are usually the simplest primary option for international tourists.
A supported cross-border wallet can be convenient for QR payments, while a modest amount of cash should be retained for smaller merchants and emergencies.
Can an e-wallet completely replace cash in Malaysia?
Not yet. Digital payments are widespread, but cash remains useful in rural areas, traditional markets and situations involving poor connectivity or unavailable payment systems.

Title: Police probe syndicate link after Malaysian held with cannabis in Chennai
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have begun investigating the syndicate network linked to a 54-year-old Malaysian detained in India with more than four kilogrammes of hydroponic cannabis.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police would work with India's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) to obtain further information on the case and trace the network involved.
"The NCID will continue to liaise with India's NCB to obtain further details of the case and investigate the syndicate network involved," he told the New Straits Times.
Hussein said the suspect, from Perak, had no previous criminal record in Malaysia.
Information from Indian authorities showed that he had travelled on Thai Airways flight TG337 from Bangkok to Chennai.
He was detained after Chennai Customs officers inspected his luggage and found about 4kg of
hydroponic cannabis
concealed inside.
Hussein said the man remained in the custody of Indian authorities and was being investigated under India's Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985 pending court proceedings.
It was previously reported that the man was detained at Chennai International Airport after allegedly attempting to smuggle 4,033g of hydroponic cannabis into India.
Chennai Customs said the passenger arrived from Bangkok and attempted to leave through the Green Channel without making a declaration.
He was stopped for inspection based on profiling, with an X-ray scan of his checked-in luggage revealing suspicious images.
Further checks uncovered four packets of cannabis concealed in a specially constructed compartment at the bottom of the luggage.
Indian authorities have warned that drug trafficking syndicates have been recruiting individuals by financing overseas travel, accommodation and other expenses before using them to transport prohibited drugs into the country.
India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence had also previously reported an increase in attempts to smuggle hydroponic cannabis from Thailand through airports in the country.
